title: Morgan Stanley's ALPHALAB: Multi-Agent Research Across Optimization Domains — Brendan Rappazzo
talk_summary: Morgan Stanley's AlphaLab is a multi-agent harness that automates quant research: a research phase builds context, a multi-agent loop builds and critiques an eval, then a strategist/worker Kanban board runs mass experiments with postmortems feeding back to the strategist. Their key lesson is that the eval/environment is the real asset, and they are moving to meta-optimizing the harness itself against strict evals.

takeaways.technique: Multi-agent eval construction with adversarial critics
takeaways.what_they_do: One agent writes the eval/backtest code, then two critic agents review it: one for conceptual errors and forward leakage, one writing unit/integration tests; issues loop back to the builder until all critics are satisfied.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one that's told to be more high-level, like are there conceptual errors in our evaluation or any kind of forward leakage of information

takeaways.what_they_do: Split review into two specialized critics rather than one general reviewer: one judges high-level correctness, the other writes concrete tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one that's more programmatic. So it's like writing unit tests and integration tests

takeaways.technique: Strategist + worker Kanban with postmortem feedback
takeaways.evidence_quote: it sort of writes this postmortem analysis, which goes back to the strategist as each job finishes

takeaways.technique: To-do list scaffolding with per-item notes to prevent early exit
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent is prompted to build a to-do list such that completing every item enables experimentation; the harness re-prompts if it tries to exit early, and each item requires markdown notes that later agents query to manage context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this allows us to kind of keep re-prompting should it try to exit early

takeaways.technique: Markdown notes as queryable shared context
takeaways.what_they_do: Each to-do item writes notes to a markdown file, and feature agents smartly query those notes to manage their context dynamically rather than carrying everything in one prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each item of the list it's instructed to build a like take notes in a markdown file

takeaways.what_they_do: They fix a strict Kaggle-style eval (data+description in, containerized model out, public/private leaderboard), then use it as a signal to hill-climb the harness manually and eventually have the LLM read traces and improve the harness itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the LLM is looking at the trace, is looking at the about, you know, the results, and improving the harness itself
